'''Michael Dunkin Penberthy''' (born November 29, 1974) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player. A [[point guard]] from [[The Master's College]] (now The Master's University), Penberthy went [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[1997 NBA draft]] but played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], winning an [[NBA championship]] in 2001. He later transitioned into coaching, serving as a shooting coach for the [[Denver Nuggets]] and an assistant coach for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

==Early life and college==
Born in [[Los Gatos, California]], Penberthy graduated from [[Herbert Hoover High School (Fresno, California)|Herbert Hoover High School]] at [[Fresno, California]] in 1993. He played college basketball for [[The Master's College]] in [[Santa Clarita, California]], where he played with distinction, broke numerous school records (including most career points), was a two-time [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] All-American, and was later a charter member of the college for the 2003–2004 season. He held the NAIA record for consecutive games with at least one three-pointer made, with 111, until it was broken in December 2005 by Brandon Cole of [[John Brown University]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2258635 NAIA star makes 3-pointer in record 112 straight games]</ref> He graduated from [[The Master's College]] in 1997 with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree in [[biblical studies]].<ref name=charter>{{cite web|title=2003-04 Charter Members|url=http://www.masters.edu/DeptPageNew.asp?PageID=1623|publisher=The Master's College|access-date=January 20, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527150119/http://www.masters.edu/DeptPageNew.asp?PageID=1623|archive-date=May 27, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Penberthy tried out for the [[Indiana Pacers]] and tore his right hamstring; he took three months off and joined the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) team [[Idaho Stampede]], which drafted him from college. The Stampede cut Penberthy, who said he "hated" playing there, without any game appearances and he transferred to the Hamburg Tigers in Germany.<ref name=SI>{{citation|last=Bias|first=Kevin C.|title=Identity Crisis|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1022261/index.htm|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=April 9, 2001|volume=94|issue=15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003142336/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1022261/index.htm|archive-date=October 3, 2009}}</ref><ref name=P-E />

During the summer of 1998, when the NBA [[1998–99 NBA lockout|locked out its players]], Penberthy worked as a forklift driver at Turf Tek, a company managed by one of his cousins. The following fall, Penberthy joined sports ministry [[Athletes in Action]] and the CBA team [[Quad City Thunder]], but was cut due to a sprained right ankle. From April to June 1999, Penberthy played for the Venezuelan team [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]].<ref name=P-E>{{cite news|last=Turner|first=Broderick|title=Lakers' shooting star|url=http://www.press-enterprise.com/newsarchive/2000/12/20/977293575.html|access-date=January 20, 2011|newspaper=Riverside Press-Enterprise|date=December 20, 2000}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="Snaidero 2007">{{cite web|title=Snaidero inks Mike Penberthy|url=http://www.euroleague.net/ulebcup/home/news/i/6862/448/snaidero-inks-mike-penberthy?smid=514|publisher=Eurocup|access-date=January 20, 2011|date=January 19, 2007}}</ref>

In his NBA career, Penberthy played in 56 games, all with the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]], and had averages of 4.9 points, 1.3 assists and 1.2 rebounds per game while playing 15.4 minutes per game on average. He won an [[NBA championship]] with the team in [[2000–01 Los Angeles Lakers season|2000–01]].

The Lakers waived Penberthy on November 10, 2001.<ref>{{cite news|last=Brown|first=Tim|title=Penberthy Becomes Victim of Numbers|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-nov-11-sp-3006-story.html|access-date=January 20, 2011|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=November 11, 2001}}</ref> Afterwards, he played basketball in Italy and Germany and competed in the [[Eurocup Basketball|ULEB Cups]] of 2005, 2006, and 2007.<ref name=Doudiz>{{cite web|title=Mike Penberthy|url=http://en.basketball.doudiz.com/player/7850/Mike-Penberthy.html|publisher=Doudiz|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110419011207/http://en.basketball.doudiz.com/player/7850/Mike-Penberthy.html|archive-date=2011-04-19}}</ref> While with Alba Berlin, Penberthy helped the team win the German Cup of 2006.<ref name="Snaidero 2007"/> In 2011, Penberthy signed with the [[Los Angeles Slam]] of the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|ABA]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://abalive.com/aba-featured-news/la-slam-acquires-former-nba-players/ |title=ABA | American Basketball Association » LA Slam Acquires Former NBA Players |access-date=2012-02-05 |archive-date=2011-12-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111219060611/http://abalive.com/aba-featured-news/la-slam-acquires-former-nba-players/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Coaching career==
In the 2014–15 season, Penberthy was the shooting coach for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-add-mike-penberthy-jason-hervey-basketball-operations-staff|title = Timberwolves Add Mike Penberthy, Jason Hervey to Basketball Operations Staff|website = [[NBA.com]]}}</ref> In the 2018–19 season, Penberthy was the shooting coach for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. On July 31, 2019, Penberthy was hired as an assistant coach for the Los Angeles Lakers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2019 |title=Lakers Announce 2019-20 Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/190730-lakers-announce-2019-20-coaching-staff |access-date=July 31, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Penberthy won his second championship when the Lakers defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2020 NBA Finals]] in six games.

In 2022, he started working as a shooting coach and pro scout for the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scouting/Player Development |url=https://cdn.nba.com/teams/uploads/sites/1610612743/2022/11/2022-23-Denver-Nuggets-Media-Guide.pdf |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=2022-23 Denver Nuggets Media Guide}}</ref>

On July 5, 2025, Penberthy joined head coach [[Jason Kidd]]'s coaching staff with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], alongside former NBA champion head coach [[Frank Vogel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mavericks add coach who worked with Jason Kidd and Frank Vogel |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/mavericks-add-coach-worked-jason-181125748.html?fr=sycsrp_catchall |website=Yahoo! Sports |date=July 5, 2025 |access-date=2025-07-06}}</ref> He left in July 2026.<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=GrantAfseth|number=2074233301242409423|title=Jay Triano, Frank Vogel, Popeye Jones, Mike Penberthy, Jordan Sears, Eric Hughes, Keith Veney, and Dru Anthrop are among the Dallas Mavericks' assistant coaches departing.|date=July 6, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Penberthy married Wendy Jones, who attended [[The Master's College]] with him and played volleyball for the college. They have three children, Ty, Jaden, and Kate.<ref name=charter />
